title: Univariate Polynomial Correctness v1
objective: Repair Sage-compatible coefficient indexing, degree, coefficient-list, derivative, and Euclidean quotient/remainder semantics across canonical ZZ[x], QQ[x], and small-prime GF(p)[x], eliminating silent None and NaN results

exceptions: Exact ZZ/QQ domains use generated FLINT resources while packed small-prime GF(p) uses a source-transparent typed-Python kernel.

handoff.summary: Implemented Sage-compatible indexing (including truncating slices), degree/list/truth predicates, resource- and kernel-backed formal derivatives, scalar // semantics, and coherent quo_rem/%/divmod across ZZ[x], QQ[x], and small-prime GF(p)[x]. Generated FLINT quotient/remainder pair resources compute once and close deterministically; the typed GF(p) kernel preserves the Python oracle. Degree-400/100 medians are 0.62ms ZZ, 3.13ms QQ, and 0.58ms GF(1009), eliminating the former ~6.2s QQ cliff. Raised the reviewed arithmetic bootstrap source budget from 575000 to 580000 bytes.
risks: Nested coefficient-ring differentiation remains outside this univariate canonical-domain slice.
The complete portable tier is currently blocked by unrelated inherited python-stdlib source-budget drift and website reference-generation failures; all polynomial-focused checks pass.
The complete native tier was stopped after package, generated FFI, production-kernel, and sanitizer lifecycle phases passed so the finished lane could be integrated promptly.
next_steps: Integrate onto dense-qq-resources and rerun repository-wide portable/native tiers after upstream budget and website drift are resolved.
Consider extending the same generated pair-resource pattern to other multi-output exact algorithms.
